thread:
maya: Quick heads-up — ran a small perf run comparing chunk-alignment heuristics for safetensors streaming vs naive byte-range reads. attaching notes.

oliver: Nice. what heuristics did you test? align-to-64MB, 1MB, or something adaptive?

maya: Tried three: fixed 64MB, fixed 4MB, and an adaptive that rounds up to containing 1..N tensors until >512KB of payload. the adaptive one beats fixed for small layers but loses on huge MLP blocks.

sam: Can you paste the command/flags you used? want to repro quickly.

maya: Sure:
```
python infra/bench/weight_warmup.py \
  --model t5x-xl \
  --format safetensors \
  --shard-size 256MB \
  --strategy adaptive --payload-threshold 524288
```

jin: Did you measure the extra disk seeks? adaptive probably increases request count for small tensors.

maya: Yes — req count went +18% vs 64MB, but total bytes read dropped ~12% and end-to-end warmstart latency at 95th improved 9% for typical seqlen workloads.

anna: Interesting. How did caching interact? i.e., if KV cache hits happen, does adaptive still help?

maya: We ran both cold and warm cache. adaptive wins on cold-starts for multi-request workloads; with warm cache the gap narrows (expected). biggest wins when layers are uneven size and many tiny tensors.

sam: Are we comfortable pushing adaptive into the loader? what's the API surface? sounds like we need a pluggable chunker.

oliver: Suggestion: expose a ChunkPolicy trait with implementations: Fixed(n), AlignToShard, Adaptive(thresholds). Loader picks policy from manifest or runtime hint. keeps backwards compat.

jin: Concern: adaptive increases metadata/manifest lookups. if we do per-tensor decision, we need efficient index-first fetches else latency explodes.

maya: Agreed. perf wins assume index-first (we had a compact index in-memory). fallback path when no index: prefer fixed 64MB alignment.

anna: Also think about eviction interplay — more small reads = more pressure on the page cache. we should simulate memory-limited instances.

maya: Good call — next run includes memory caps. early results: under 4GB mem the adaptive policy flips and fixed 64MB wins due to more churn.

sam: So policy should be aware of available memory + workload distribution. maybe a runtime hint: prefer_low_memory: true/false.

oliver: That starts getting complex. alternative: let the scheduler decide per-request strategy based on target SLO (latency vs bandwidth).

maya: For rollout plan: implement ChunkPolicy interface + adaptive impl behind a feature flag. default to legacy fixed alignment for Dedicated/Private until we have evict sims.

jin: Can we add telemetry keys: chunk_policy, bytes_read, num_seeks, warmstart_p95. We need to correlate with evictions.

maya: Will add metrics. also adding a small YAML snippet for manifest hints:
```
chunk_policy: adaptive
payload_threshold: 524288
prefer_low_memory: false
```

deploy-bot: deploy queued: feature/loader-chunk-policy -> staging (canary 10% traffic)

anna: Awesome. If you want help with the mem-cap sim, I can wire up microvm runs.

maya: Please do. I'll push the PR with the trait + adaptive impl and unit tests later today. thanks all :rocket:
